messages.author: 3268b1ddfb2eb06a
messages.subject: Parser Error after changing to new notation
parts:
I recently upgraded to rstan v2.11.1 and when I ran some previously functional code, I received warnings about changing "<-" to "=", "_log" to "_lpdf" etc. I updated my code accordingly, and now I get this error:


SYNTAX ERROR, MESSAGE(S) FROM PARSER:


ERROR at line 37

 35:      logl = 0.0;
 36:      for (i in 1:n){
 37:        s = log(dCphi_du1du2_s(normal_cdf(y1[i] | mu1[i], sigma1), logistic_cdf(z[i] | mu2[i], 1), phi)) + normal_lpdf(y1[i] | mu1[i], sigma1) + logistic_lpdf(z[i] | mu2[i], 1);
                                                ^
 38:        logl = logl + s;

PARSER EXPECTED: "("
Error in stanc(file = file, model_code = model_code, model_name = model_name,  :
  failed to parse Stan model 'FB_frank' due to the above error.


Here is the offending code block (it is part of the functions block):


real copulapdf_lpdf(real[] y1, real[] z, vector mu1, vector mu2, real sigma1, real phi, int n){
  real logl;
  real s;
  logl = 0.0;
  for (i in 1:n){
    s = log(dCphi_du1du2_s(normal_cdf(y1[i] | mu1[i], sigma1), logistic_cdf(z[i] | mu2[i], 1), phi)) + normal_lpdf(y1[i] | mu1[i], sigma1) + logistic_lpdf(z[i] | mu2[i], 1);
    logl = logl + s;
  }
  return logl;
}


dCphi_du1du2_s() is another function that I have defined:


real dCphi_du2_s(real u1, real u2, real phi) {
  real b;
  real a;
  b = exp(phi*(u1+u2)) - exp(phi*(1+u2)) - exp(phi*(1+u1)) + exp(phi);
  a = -exp(phi)*(exp(phi*u1) - 1)/b;
  return a;
}


The rest of the code:

data {
  int<lower=0> n; // number of subjects
  int<lower=0> k1; // number of predictors for y1
  int<lower=0> k2; // number of predictors for y2
  real y1[n]; // continuous data
  real y2[n]; // 0/1 binary data
  matrix[n, k1] x1; // predictor variables for y1
  matrix[n, k2] x2; // predictor variables for y2
}

transformed data{
  int<lower=-1, upper=1> sign[n];
  for (i in 1:n) {
    if (y2[i]==1)
      sign[i] = 1;
    else
      sign[i] = -1;
  }
}

parameters {
  real phi; // frank copula param
  vector[k1] b1; // beta coefficients for y1
  vector[k2] b2; // beta coefficients for y2
  real<lower=0> abs_z[n]; // abs value of latent variable
  real<lower=0> sigma1; // sd for y1's normal distribution
}

transformed parameters {
  real v[n];
  vector[n] mu1; // location for y1
  vector[n] mu2; // location for z
  for (i in 1:n) {
    v[i] = sign[i] * abs_z[i];
  }
  mu1 = x1 * b1;
  mu2 = x2 * b2;
}

model {
  b1 ~ normal(0, 100);
  b2 ~ normal(0, 100);
  phi ~ normal(0, 10);
  target += copulapdf_lpdf(y1, v, mu1, mu2, sigma1, phi, n);
}


Thank you in advance for the help!

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Parser Error after changing to new notation
parts:
That fragment looks OK to me, but we can't really diagnose
syntactic problems without the whole program.

Also, good formatting can really help understand the layout,
such as:

> s = log(dCphi_du1du2_s(normal_cdf(y1[i] | mu1[i], sigma1),
> logistic_cdf(z[i] | mu2[i], 1),
> phi))
> + normal_lpdf(y1[i] | mu1[i], sigma1)
> + logistic_lpdf(z[i] | mu2[i], 1);

It also makes it easier for others (including you in the future)
to read your code.

- Bob

p <- 2

dat <- list(y1=y1, y2=y2, x1=x1, x2=x2, k1=p, k2=p, n=N)
fit <- stan(file = 'FB_frank.stan', data=dat, iter=500, chains=2, thin=1, warmup=100)

I have attached the stan file. You should be able to reproduce the error with this.

Thanks,
Ved

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Parser Error after changing to new notation
parts:
Hi Ved,

For *_cdf() functions, you'll need a comma between the first and second arguments.
If you use *_lcdf() functions, you'll use |.

If you fix that, you'll run into a problem with the lpdf function later on.


Daniel

parts:
Sorry, that's a bug with the new notation that has already
been patched on the develop branch (so it will go in the next
release).

https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/issues/1944

For now, I'm afraid you have to use the old notation.

We take these notation changes very seriously and spent a long
time thinking about the new notation, and have no plans to change
any of our notation in the future.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Parser Error after changing to new notation
parts: Thanks, Bob.

> On Aug 19, 2016, at 11:33 AM, Bob Carpenter <ca...@alias-i.com> wrote:
>
> Sorry, that's a bug with the new notation that has already
> been patched on the develop branch (so it will go in the next
> release).
>
> https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/issues/1944
>
> For now, I'm afraid you have to use the old notation.
>
> We take these notation changes very seriously and spent a long
> time thinking about the new notation, and have no plans to change
> any of our notation in the future.
>
> - Bob
>
>
>> On Aug 19, 2016, at 5:25 PM, Ved Deshpande <ved.de...@uconn.edu> wrote:
>>
>> Hi Daniel,
>>
>> I added the vertical bar as per your suggestion in the model block:
>>
>> target += copulapdf_lpdf(y1 | v, mu1, mu2, sigma1, phi, n);
>>
>> I now get this strange error:
>>
>> Error in compileCode(f, code, language = language, verbose = verbose) :
>> Compilation ERROR, function(s)/method(s) not created! file13504516527e.cpp: In instantiation of ‘T__ model135055e84018_FB_frank_namespace::model135055e84018_FB_frank::log_prob(std::vector<T2>&, std::vector<int>&, std::ostream*) const [with bool propto__ = true; bool jacobian__ = true; T__ = stan::math::var; std::ostream = std::basic_ostream<char>]’:
>> /home/ved/R/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu-library/3.3/StanHeaders/include/src/stan/model/util.hpp:108:39: required from ‘double stan::model::log_prob_grad(const M&, std::vector<double>&, std::vector<int>&, std::vector<double>&, std::ostream*) [with bool propto = true; bool jacobian_adjust_transform = true; M = model135055e84018_FB_frank_namespace::model135055e84018_FB_frank; std::ostream = std::basic_ostream<char>]’
>> /home/ved/R/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu-library/3.3/rstan/include/rstan/stan_fit.hpp:1464:51: required from ‘SEXPREC* rstan::stan_fit<Model, RNG_t>::grad_log_prob(SEXP, SEXP) [with Model = model135055e84018_FB_frank_namesp
>> In addition: Warning message:
>> running command '/usr/lib/R/bin/R CMD SHLIB file13504516527e.cpp 2> file13504516527e.cpp.err.txt' had status 1
>>
>> Any clues as to what is going on?
>>
>> On Friday, August 19, 2016 at 8:18:25 PM UTC+5:30, Daniel Lee wrote:
>> The | is always between the first and second arguments.
>>
>> You're evaluating the value the value of a density, copulapdf_lpdf(), of y1 given all the other arguments.
>>
>>
>> Daniel
>>
>>
>> On Fri, Aug 19, 2016 at 10:45 AM, Ved Deshpande <ved.de...@uconn.edu> wrote:
>> Hi Daniel,
>>
>> Indeed, after fixing the *_cdf() functions, I run into the error:
>>
>> ERROR at line 70
>>
>> 68: b2 ~ normal(0, 100);
>> 69: phi ~ normal(0, 10);
>> 70: target += copulapdf_lpdf(y1, v, mu1, mu2, sigma1, phi, n);
>> ^
>> 71: }
>>
>> PARSER EXPECTED: <probability function arguments>
>>
>> which probably means that I have to put a | somewhere in copulapdf_lpdf(). Now, amongst the arguments of copulapdf_lpdf():
>>
>> - y1, n are in the data block
>> - v, mu1 and mu2 are in the transformed parameters block
>> - sigma1, phi are in the parameters block
>>
>> Conceptually, copulapdf_lpdf() is the bivariate probability density on y1 (which is data) and v(a latent variable). So, where should the | go?
>>
>> On Friday, August 19, 2016 at 7:53:10 PM UTC+5:30, Daniel Lee wrote:
>> Hi Ved,
>>
>> For *_cdf() functions, you'll need a comma between the first and second arguments.
>> If you use *_lcdf() functions, you'll use |.
>>
>> If you fix that, you'll run into a problem with the lpdf function later on.
>>
>>
>> Daniel
>>
>>
>> On Fri, Aug 19, 2016 at 10:13 AM, Ved Deshpande <ved.de...@uconn.edu> wrote:
>> Thanks Bob. Here is a MWE:
>>
>> set.seed(0)
>> N <- 100
>> p <- 2
>> y1 <- rnorm(N)
>> y2 <- sample(0:1, N, replace=TRUE)
>> x1 <- x2 <- matrix(rnorm(N*p), N)
>> dat <- list(y1=y1, y2=y2, x1=x1, x2=x2, k1=p, k2=p, n=N)
>> fit <- stan(file = 'FB_frank.stan', data=dat, iter=500, chains=2, thin=1, warmup=100)
>>
>> I have attached the stan file. You should be able to reproduce the error with this.
>>
>> Thanks,
>> Ved
>>
>>
>> On Friday, August 19, 2016 at 5:31:16 PM UTC+5:30, Bob Carpenter wrote:
>> That fragment looks OK to me, but we can't really diagnose
>> syntactic problems without the whole program.
>>
>> Also, good formatting can really help understand the layout,
>> such as:
>>
>>> s = log(dCphi_du1du2_s(normal_cdf(y1[i] | mu1[i], sigma1),
>>> logistic_cdf(z[i] | mu2[i], 1),
>>> phi))
>>> + normal_lpdf(y1[i] | mu1[i], sigma1)
>>> + logistic_lpdf(z[i] | mu2[i], 1);
>>
>> It also makes it easier for others (including you in the future)
>> to read your code.
>>
>> - Bob
>>
